title: Tech's biggest moves this week

slides.headline: Tech's biggest moves this week
slides.subtitle: From streaming price hikes to border privacy, here is what matters in tech today.

slides.headline: Trump targets EU tech fines
slides.explanation: The US president is vowing to investigate the EU over antitrust fines against major American tech firms. He argues that penalties against companies like Google and Apple should be entirely reversed.

slides.headline: The mystery of the OpenAI hack
slides.explanation: Security researchers at Hugging Face say an AI performed a hack at superhuman speed with almost no human help. Experts are debating whether this represents a major new threat or just a publicity stunt.

slides.headline: Roku raises hardware prices
slides.explanation: Roku has quietly increased the price of its streaming devices, with some models now costing up to $50 more. This change impacts their entire lineup, including the entry-level streaming sticks.

slides.headline: Paramount and WBD merger stalled
slides.explanation: A planned merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery is on hold for months while a lawsuit moves to trial. The New York Attorney General called the pause a critical victory for the case.

slides.headline: Border phone search sparks legal fight
slides.explanation: A US citizen is challenging government claims that he wiped his phone during a border inspection using a secret duress password. The case is raising new questions about privacy rights when traveling.

caption:
From streaming price hikes to major shifts in tech policy, here are the stories you need to know today. Which of these headlines caught your attention the most?

title: Trump's Big Moves at Home and Abroad

slides.headline: Trump's Big Moves at Home and Abroad
slides.subtitle: From energy grants to trade threats, here is what you need to know today.

slides.headline: Clean energy grants denied to states
slides.explanation: Court documents reveal the Trump administration blocked billions in clean energy funding for states that did not support his re-election. This raises serious questions about how federal money is distributed based on political loyalty.

slides.headline: New tariff threats against the EU
slides.explanation: Donald Trump is threatening major tariffs on the European Union after Brussels fined American tech giants. This could lead to a massive trade dispute that impacts prices for consumers on both sides of the Atlantic.

slides.headline: US expands military strikes on Iran
slides.explanation: The US has launched attacks on targets across Iran in response to regional drone strikes. The escalation marks a dangerous shift as the conflict spreads across the Middle East.

slides.headline: Zelensky faces political fallout
slides.explanation: President Zelensky is dealing with protests and criticism after firing his defense minister. Observers are watching to see if this move weakens his political standing during the ongoing war.

slides.headline: White House dinner finally takes place
slides.explanation: The White House Correspondents' Association dinner is finally happening after being delayed by a security threat months ago. It is a rare moment of normalcy in a busy week for Washington.

caption:
It is a busy news cycle with major developments in trade, energy, and foreign policy. From shifting alliances to internal political tension, there is a lot to keep track of this week. Which of these stories do you think will have the biggest impact long term?
